w: Swamishri, during his address to the youths of Kisumu, advised, "It was the wish of Yogiji Maharaj that if the youths are awake and wedded to Satsang then there will be a better society. You must remember that whatever you do in Satsang is to please Shriji Maharaj and for one’s salvation and not for praise or appreciation... Yogiji Maharaj gave the formula of unity and harmony. If you have harmony, friendliness and unity then you can accomplish whatever work you wish... Here in Satsang the fruits of a minor or major seva are the same. Firstly, if your faith and observance of moral codes is firm and unswerving then others will have trust in you. Secondly, you should attend the weekly Sunday assembly, do your puja daily, come for mandir darshan and regularly read the Vachanamrit and Swami ni Vato..."

The whole world needs harmony, friendliness and unity. (Samp, Suhradbhav, Ekta). Every person needs it. Politics needs it and society too needs it. And we especially need it because we have come for moksha.
One should have an eye for glory (mahima). If someone scolds you then don’t bring it to mind. Say sorry or Jay Swaminarayan and like a line in water, forget it.

Success lies in having single faith and refuge in God and doing whatever the holy sadhu says. The Pandavas faced insurmountable difficulties and obstacles but still they survived and were redeemed. They triumphed in the Mahabharat war and earned the grace of God.
Swamishri performed the murti pratishtha at the Shree Swaminarayan Mandir, Clifton.

In the evening assembly a memorable program by children was performed before an audience of 16,000 devotees. Firstly, a saga of outstanding children of the Bal Mandal was narrated. It reflected the effect of Satsang on their moral, social and academic performances. Then young children chanted the dhun and told Swamishri to play the dholak and chant the dhun. This was followed by an impressive monoacting presentation on the story of Magniram. The children also took the opportunity of playing 'ras' with Swamishri and then performed arti and offered thal to Thakorji. Finally, the program was crowned with Swamishri's blessings.

Bal/Balika Din After the presentation by balaks in the evening satsang assembly, Swamishri blessed the audience, “Our true wealth is that our children imbibe good virtues and spirituality. For this the parents have to be extremely alert. There should be a mandir in the home. But nowadays there is a TV instead of a mandir. And they watch that which should not be watched. They sit together and watch. Then how will respect (for elders) remain? With this loss of respect, the family is destroyed. One sees all this, yet one does not think to stop. Only when one understands this and practices it will one experience happiness.”

The 221st birthday anniversary of Gunatitanand Swami was celebrated in the mandir hall. The celebration assembly was themed on the importance of Gunatitanand Swami’s presence on earth. Speeches on Gunatitanand Swami as an ideal sadhu, an inspirer of God-realization in devotees, and the promoter of supreme upasana were made by sadhus. Thereafter a drama, “Abhaysinh’s Resoluteness”, was performed in Swamishri’s presence. Viveksagar Swami discoursed about the eternal presence of the Gunatit Sadhu. Then the youths of Mumbai performed a traditional dance. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly, “Shriji Maharaj said that he had come on earth with his abode, Gunatit. He brought his abode with him because he wanted all to attain the gunatit state – free of all desires – and liberate them from root-ignorance. It is because of body-consciousness (dehbhav) that one remains ignorant. Till one does not realize one’s original form (i.e. One must perform one’s worldly duties, but one’s mind should be engaged in God.” At 7.45 pm Swamishri performed the celebration arti.

st.t: BAPS News – BAPS Centenary Celebrations, UK & Europe – Wembley Arena, London, Sunday 7 October 2007
w: The grand centenary celebrations of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha for UK and Europe were held at one of London’s most prestigious venues, Wembley Arena, on Sunday 7 October 2007 in the presence of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

The programme was witnessed by almost 12,000 invited guests and dignitaries. Thousands also gathered at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Neasden, who watched via a live telecast. And many more from around the world enjoyed the live webcast.

The opening abstract video set the tone of the event, introducing the concept of serving others. This was elaborated upon with testimonies from young and old volunteers of BAPS and how they had been inspired to work for the joy of others.
A spectacular welcome dance enthralled the capacity audience, who also contributed to the joyous mood by clapping and waving their flags.

Thereafter, the origin of the concept of ‘In the joy of others, lies our own’ was traced to ancient Hindu scriptures. This was followed by senior sadhus who spoke of the rich history of service in BAPS, narrating it from the life and work of Bhagwan Swaminarayan through to Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. These short addresses were complemented by inspiring video presentations and then another energetic dance.

A recounting of the history of service in the organisation was followed by a presentation about current BAPS activities and live testimonies. This further enhanced the message of finding our own joy in the joy of others. In continuation of this theme and as a part of its ongoing multifarious community outreach programmes, BAPS took this opportunity to raise funds and awareness for Breast Cancer Care, UK. Proceeds from voluntary donations were pledged to the worthy cause, with BAPS presenting a first cheque of £12,000 on the day.

Another special feature of the evening’s programme was the message from the Prime Minister, Rt. Hon. Gordon Brown MP . He congratulated and thanked BAPS on its hundred years of service to the community, and added: “The contribution you make to the education of our young people and the cultural community life of London and the United Kingdom is something you all should be very proud of. You espouse ideals of community and voluntary service, which are an example to us all.” Several MPs, local councillors and local leaders were also honoured.

Then after collective prayers by children, youths and the elderly, Swamishri offered his blessings for the auspicious occasion by emphasising the progress of spirituality through the scriptures. Finally, Swamishri encouraged family harmony and spoke of the messages of Bhagwan Swaminarayan to serve for the good of others, and prayed that we endeavour to serve for the joy of others.

The grand finale of the occasion came with a glorious centenary dance, which climaxed with streams of confetti erupting inside the auditorium and providing a memorable conclusion to this breathtaking celebration.
When Pramukh Swami Maharaj arrived at the Rupchoki, all the sadhus sang, "Then Shyamsundar spoke, go, I have granted you that boon."
Nilkanthseva Swami said, "What will you give?"
Viratswarup Swami said, "Give us Akshardham."

Swamishri said, "You have my blessings. Since we have become sadhus, become the very best sadhus. May your observance of niyam and dharma, and of agna and upasana, become firm. Build such a life that others too get the impression that these are the very best sadhus. We have to live a life that pleases Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. We want to become as they would like us to be. We want to give up whatever they do not like. We have to act according to their wishes. Even if someone scolds or insults us, it should not matter. We should think that we are sadhus. If there is such saintliness, it will make an impression. No other adornment of ours will be of any use. Whatever glory there is, is only because of saintliness. So keep your focus on that. No rajasic tendencies at all. Although they are not there, take special care of this. Keep the aim that they never creep in. Keeping all this firm, work together in unity."
Swamishri showed a wonderful goal for life.

ds.t: The lazy man and the date
w: Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to the Smruti Mandir. Here the sadhus gave a special presentation. In Yogiji Maharaj's parables there is a story of a lazy man. A lazy man was sleeping under a ber (jujube) tree. A ber fell from the tree and landed right on his navel. The lazy man felt like eating the ber, but he was too lazy to move his hand to his navel and then bring it back to his mouth. So he asked a traveller passing on the road to put the ber in his mouth for him. That is how lazy people are.

The sadhus gave a presentation of this kind here. Here Aksharatit Swami lay as the lazy man with his belly bare. A date had fallen on his belly. Whoever walked by, he asked them to put that date in his mouth.
In this way Hariprakash Swami came by as the traveller and asked, "What do you want?"
He said, "Please put the date lying on my belly into my mouth!"
On hearing this, the traveller became irritated and said, "You king of the lazy! What effort is it for you to do that much?"
Swamishri, who had been listening, immediately addressed Hariprakash Swami and said, "But what effort is it for you?"

Swamishri's twist was wonderful. Only one who can help each person even after knowing their nature, temperament and limitations can be a true servant of society. Such selfless feeling is in Swamishri's heart, and so these words naturally came from Swamishri's lips.
After completing the pradakshina (circumambulation), as Swamishri was coming down the slope, Hariprakash Swami said to him, "When will he understand?"
Swamishri said, "But you have understood, haven't you?"
This sentence too was wonderful. These very feelings lie at the root of Swamishri's compassion. Only such a feeling can give love to everyone and love selflessly.

Bhupatbhai and Rajubhai had come from Ranpur for darshan. Bhupatbhai's sons, who now run a factory, were also with them. When they were introduced to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Swamishri, chanting "Swaminarayan" as if turning a mala, said, "Just as you run that factory, you should also run this factory (of bhajan). Then that factory will also run a quarter better."

Today, showering blessings in the Gurubhakti Din (Day of Devotion to the Guru) assembly, Guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj said: "Obstinacy, ego and jealousy take one very far from Satsang. Phaiba, what was the problem? She did all kinds of seva! But she did not have in her mind, 'I want to please Maharaj', so what was the result? Maharaj went to Machhiyav 32 times. So it would rank first among the five pilgrim places, but after Maharaj abandoned it, no sadhus or devotees ever went there. If one has other faults, one can slowly reach moksha, but if one has these three, one is thrown out. Alaiyakhachar was thrown out through ego and Jivakhachar through jealousy. Whatever we do, before taking the first step, we should think, 'Is Swami pleased?' If yes, go ahead. If in doubt, stop, and if he is not pleased, turn back. Seen this way, Satsang is very easy."
